title: Write a Rolling Patch Playbook in Ansible
intro: servers-incident-002 happened because every server patched and rebooted on its own schedule, all at the same minute. Write the replacement: one playbook that patches the web fleet a quarter at a time, reboots only when needed, and stops if anything goes wrong.

steps.prompt:
Write patch.yml with one play:
- name: Patch web servers; hosts: web; become: true
- serial: "25%" and max_fail_percentage: 0
- tasks:
  1. ansible.builtin.apt with upgrade: dist and update_cache: true
  2. ansible.builtin.stat on path /var/run/reboot-required, register: reboot_required
  3. ansible.builtin.reboot with reboot_timeout: 600, only when: reboot_required.stat.exists
  4. ansible.builtin.uri to url http://localhost/healthz expecting status_code: 200 (a health check after each host)
steps.hint:
Top-level structure:
- name: Patch web servers
  hosts: web
  become: true
  serial: "25%"
  max_fail_percentage: 0
  tasks:
    - name: Upgrade packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        upgrade: dist
        update_cache: true
    ... then the stat / reboot (with 'when:') / uri tasks, in that order.
steps.solution:
- name: Patch web servers
  hosts: web
  become: true
  serial: "25%"
  max_fail_percentage: 0
  tasks:
    - name: Upgrade all packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        upgrade: dist
        update_cache: true

    - name: Check whether a reboot is required
      ansible.builtin.stat:
        path: /var/run/reboot-required
      register: reboot_required

    - name: Reboot if required
      ansible.builtin.reboot:
        reboot_timeout: 600
      when: reboot_required.stat.exists

    - name: Verify the host is healthy before moving on
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: http://localhost/healthz
        status_code: 200
steps.fake_output:
playbook: patch.yml

PLAY [Patch web servers] ***** (batch 1/4)
TASK [Upgrade all packages] ***  changed: [web-01] changed: [web-02]
TASK [Check whether a reboot is required] ***  ok: [web-01] ok: [web-02]
TASK [Reboot if required] ***  changed: [web-01] skipping: [web-02]
TASK [Verify the host is healthy before moving on] ***  ok: [web-01] ok: [web-02]
...
PLAY RECAP ***  web-01..web-08: failed=0
steps.explanation: A quarter of the fleet at a time. Each host is patched, rebooted only if the kernel or core libraries need it, and health-checked before the next batch starts.
steps.why: Every line maps to a failure it prevents. serial limits the blast radius; max_fail_percentage: 0 stops the rollout at the first unhealthy host instead of breaking the whole fleet (servers-tutorial-003); the stat-then-conditional reboot avoids needless reboots; and the health check makes 'rebooted' mean 'serving again' before Ansible moves on. In production you'd add a pre_task that drains the host from the load balancer and a post_task that re-adds it, and you'd run this from CI with an approval, never from a laptop (servers-incident-005).
